sm: Judicial Watch reports that records unsealed on November twenty-third by Chief Judge James Boasberg reveal a broad federal criminal investigation of Representative Ilhan Omar over the search of her Washington home on October twelfth. The warrant covers conduct from 1980 to the present, and the specific statutes are redacted. More than half of the 169 released pages are entirely blacked out. Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh held the warrant for a week, raised Speech or Debate Clause concerns himself, required a special search protocol, and signed it on October ninth. Senior Justice Department officials were involved, agents could seize phones and computers, and the Justice Department said in November that the investigation remains active and the warrant is not fully executed.

This part says the Justice Department cited an earlier, broader warrant against a person whose name is redacted, one that had no special Speech or Debate procedures, to argue for fewer protections for Omar. Judicial Watch says the earlier target may be a current or former member of Congress. It calls the release an initial victory and says it will ask the court to unseal the suspected crimes. The group filed its unsealing motion on October fifteenth, and a hearing was held November seventeenth. It also recalls a 2019 ethics complaint about Omar and its past success in unsealing the Mar-a-Lago affidavit in August 2022.

Judicial Watch notes that in August 2026 a federal court unsealed records on the FBI's 2022 seizure of Mike Lindell's phone. They show the FBI relied partly on Dominion Voting Systems' 1.3 billion dollar defamation suit against Lindell. The rest of this part is a Thanksgiving message. It recounts the Pilgrims' hard first year at Plymouth, the 1621 harvest feast shared with Massasoit and about ninety of his men, and the 1800s origin of the First Thanksgiving story. It reflects on gratitude and quotes the hymn We Gather Together, and ends with Thanksgiving wishes from the organization.
